details: Oil prices rose as geopolitical tensions escalated in the Middle East, with reports of renewed Iranian drone and missile attacks on commercial tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. This situation raises concerns about energy supply disruptions and persistent supply-side inflation, impacting global markets.
title: Mideast Tensions Fuel Oil Price Hike Amid Strait of Hormuz Attacks

details: Kristalina Georgieva, the Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund, warned that the global economy faces threats from persistently high energy prices, record public debt, and risks associated with the artificial intelligence investment boom. She noted that conflicts in the Middle East contribute to a negative energy supply shock.
title: IMF Chief Highlights Energy Shock, Debt, AI Risks to Global Growth

details: The U.S. government transferred approximately 17,795 Bitcoin, valued at about $1.5 billion, to Coinbase Prime over October 7-8, 2026. These transfers, originating from government-linked wallets, are significant as the market awaits Washington's plans for these confiscated assets, which amount to roughly $27-28 billion in total holdings.
title: US Government Moves 17,795 Bitcoin to Coinbase Prime

details: The total cryptocurrency market capitalization decreased by 3% on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, erasing approximately $88 billion in value. This decline, which saw Bitcoin fall to $84,100, was attributed to a macro-driven risk reversal, tightening financial conditions, dollar strength, and rising bond yields rather than crypto-specific catalysts.
title: Crypto Market Cap Falls 3% on October 7 Due to Macro Reversal

details: TOKEN2049, the world's largest crypto conference, announced its expansion to the United States with the launch of TOKEN2049 New York. The inaugural US edition is scheduled for June 16-17, 2027, expecting 15,000 attendees, establishing New York as a permanent fixture on its annual event circuit alongside Singapore and Dubai.
title: TOKEN2049, World's Largest Crypto Conference, Expands to New York

details: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is nearing the October 20, 2026, deadline for public comments on its "Regulation Crypto Assets" proposal. This significant regulatory framework could reshape how cryptocurrency projects raise capital and operate under federal securities laws, introducing registration exemptions and a conditional safe harbor.
title: SEC's "Regulation Crypto Assets" Comment Period Closes October 20
